resource.name: aws_route53_record
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_route53_record` resource enables the creation and management of DNS records within Amazon Route 53, supporting a wide range of record types such as A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, and more. It is commonly used for configuring domain name resolution, setting up subdomains, routing traffic to AWS services (e.g., S3, CloudFront, ELB), and implementing failover or geolocation-based routing. This resource allows users to define TTL, alias targets, weighted routing, and health checks, making it essential for scalable, reliable, and customized DNS management in cloud environments.

examples.title: Simple routing policy
examples.code:
resource "aws_route53_record" "www" {
  zone_id = aws_route53_zone.primary.zone_id
  name    = "www.example.com"
  type    = "A"
  ttl     = 300
  records = [aws_eip.lb.public_ip]
}
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an AWS Route 53 record with a simple routing policy, using the `aws_route53_record` resource to create an A record that maps a domain name (`www.example.com`) to the public IP of an Elastic IP (`aws_eip.lb.public_ip`). Key configurations include specifying the `zone_id`, `type`, `ttl`, and `records` arguments to enable straightforward DNS resolution for a web application.

examples.title: Weighted routing policy
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure weighted routing policies for AWS Route 53 records using the `aws_route53_record` resource. It illustrates the use of the `weighted_routing_policy` block to distribute traffic between two CNAME records (`dev.example.com` and `live.example.com`) with different weights (10 and 90), enabling traffic balancing based on predefined proportions.

examples.title: Geoproximity routing policy
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an `aws_route53_record` resource with a geoproximity routing policy, enabling location-based DNS routing using latitude and longitude coordinates. It showcases the use of the `geoproximity_routing_policy` block, `coordinates` sub-block, and `set_identifier` for targeted traffic management, along with a CNAME record setup for a specific environment.

examples.title: Alias record
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an AWS Route 53 alias record (`aws_route53_record`) to point to an Elastic Load Balancer (`aws_elb`) using the `alias` block. It showcases key arguments such as `name`, `zone_id`, and `evaluate_target_health`, enabling users to set up DNS routing for a domain (`example.com`) with health evaluation targeting an ELB.

examples.title: Alias record for AWS Global Accelerator
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates how to configure an AWS Route 53 alias record (`aws_route53_record`) to point to an AWS Global Accelerator using the `alias` block, showcasing key arguments like `name`, `zone_id`, and `evaluate_target_health` for seamless DNS routing to a globally distributed application."

examples.title: NS and SOA Record Management
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates how to configure an AWS Route 53 NS (Name Server) record with the `aws_route53_record` resource, using the `allow_overwrite` argument and dynamically referencing name servers from an associated Route 53 hosted zone. This example illustrates NS record management for delegating DNS authority to specific name servers."

arguments.name: allow_overwrite
arguments.description: (Optional) Allow creation of this record in Terraform to overwrite an existing record, if any. This does not affect the ability to update the record in Terraform and does not prevent other resources within Terraform or manual Route 53 changes outside Terraform from overwriting this record. `false` by default. This configuration is not recommended for most environments. Exactly one of records or alias must be specified: this determines whether it's an alias record.
arguments.llm_summary: The `allow_overwrite` argument in the `aws_route53_record` resource controls whether Terraform can overwrite an existing DNS record in Route 53 during creation. Setting this to `true` enables users to replace pre-existing records without manual deletion, which can be useful for managing dynamic or evolving DNS configurations, but it is generally discouraged in stable environments to avoid unintended overwrites.

arguments.name: health_check_id
arguments.description: (Optional) The health check the record should be associated with.
arguments.llm_summary: The `health_check_id` argument in the `aws_route53_record` resource allows users to associate the DNS record with a specific Route 53 health check, enabling automated monitoring and failover based on the health status of the target resource. By configuring this argument, users can enhance reliability and ensure traffic is routed only to healthy endpoints, supporting goals like high availability and fault tolerance.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument in the `aws_route53_record` resource represents the unique identifier for the Route 53 record, typically auto-generated by Terraform and AWS. While not required to be explicitly set by the user, it can be used to reference or track the record within Terraform configurations and outputs, aiding in resource management and debugging.

arguments.name: multivalue_answer_routing_policy
arguments.description: (Optional) Set to `true` to indicate a multivalue answer routing policy. Conflicts with any other routing policy.
arguments.llm_summary: The `multivalue_answer_routing_policy` argument in the `aws_route53_record` resource allows users to enable multivalue answer routing, which returns multiple IP addresses in response to DNS queries, improving availability and load distribution across resources. Setting this to `true` configures the record to use this routing policy, but it cannot be combined with other routing policies, ensuring focused control over DNS query behavior.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Required) The name of the record.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name` argument in the `aws_route53_record` resource specifies the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) for the DNS record being created or managed. By defining this argument, users control the exact hostname or subdomain that the record will resolve to, enabling the configuration of DNS entries for services, applications, or infrastructure endpoints.

arguments.name: records
arguments.description: (Required for non-alias records) A string list of records. To specify a single record value longer than 255 characters such as a TXT record for DKIM, add `\"\"` inside the Terraform configuration string (e.g., `"first255characters\"\"morecharacters"`).
arguments.llm_summary: The `records` argument in the `aws_route53_record` resource allows users to define the specific DNS record values associated with a non-alias Route 53 record, such as IP addresses, CNAMEs, or TXT entries. By configuring this argument, users can specify the data returned in DNS queries for the record, enabling functionality like domain name resolution, email authentication (e.g., DKIM), or service discovery.

arguments.name: set_identifier
arguments.description: (Optional) Unique identifier to differentiate records with routing policies from one another. Required if using `cidr_routing_policy`, `failover_routing_policy`, `geolocation_routing_policy`,`geoproximity_routing_policy`, `latency_routing_policy`, `multivalue_answer_routing_policy`, or `weighted_routing_policy`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `set_identifier` argument in the `aws_route53_record` resource allows users to define a unique string identifier for DNS records that use advanced routing policies, such as failover, geolocation, latency, or weighted routing. By specifying this identifier, users can differentiate and manage multiple records within the same domain name, enabling precise control over traffic routing and policy-based DNS behavior.

arguments.name: ttl
arguments.description: (Required for non-alias records) The TTL of the record.
arguments.llm_summary: The `ttl` argument in the `aws_route53_record` resource specifies the Time-to-Live (TTL) value for non-alias DNS records, defining how long the record's information is cached by DNS resolvers. Configuring this value allows users to control the frequency of DNS updates, balancing responsiveness to changes with reduced query overhead.

arguments.name: type
arguments.description: (Required) The record type. Valid values are `A`, `AAAA`, `CAA`, `CNAME`, `DS`, `MX`, `NAPTR`, `NS`, `PTR`, `SOA`, `SPF`, `SRV` and `TXT`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `type` argument in the `aws_route53_record` resource specifies the DNS record type, allowing users to define the behavior and purpose of the record within a Route 53 hosted zone. By setting this required argument to values like `A`, `CNAME`, or `MX`, users control how the record resolves queries, enabling functionality such as IP address mapping, domain aliasing, email routing, or service-specific configurations.

arguments.name: zone_id
arguments.description: (Required) The ID of the hosted zone to contain this record.
arguments.llm_summary: The `zone_id` argument specifies the unique identifier of the Route 53 hosted zone where the DNS record will be created, enabling users to associate the record with the correct DNS namespace. This is a required parameter that ensures the record is properly scoped to the intended hosted zone, supporting accurate domain name resolution and DNS management.

blocks.name: alias
blocks.description: (Optional) An alias block. Conflicts with `ttl` & `records`. Documented below.

arguments.name: evaluate_target_health
arguments.description: (Required) Set to `true` if you want Route 53 to determine whether to respond to DNS queries using this resource record set by checking the health of the resource record set. Some resources have special requirements, see related part of documentation.
arguments.llm_summary: The `evaluate_target_health` argument in the `alias` block of the `aws_route53_record` resource controls whether Route 53 checks the health of the target resource before responding to DNS queries. Setting this to `true` enables health-based routing, ensuring DNS responses are only provided if the target resource is healthy, which is critical for high availability and failover configurations.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Required) DNS domain name for a CloudFront distribution, S3 bucket, ELB, AWS Global Accelerator, or another resource record set in this hosted zone.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name` argument specifies the DNS domain name associated with the alias target, such as a CloudFront distribution, S3 bucket, ELB, AWS Global Accelerator, or another resource record set within the hosted zone. By defining this required value, users establish the primary identifier for routing traffic to the intended resource, enabling seamless DNS resolution and integration with AWS services.

arguments.name: zone_id
arguments.description: (Required) Hosted zone ID for a CloudFront distribution, S3 bucket, ELB, AWS Global Accelerator, or Route 53 hosted zone. See `resource_elb.zone_id` for example.
arguments.llm_summary: The `zone_id` argument specifies the hosted zone ID associated with the target resource (e.g., CloudFront distribution, S3 bucket, ELB, AWS Global Accelerator, or Route 53 hosted zone) for an alias record in Route 53. By defining this value, users ensure the alias record correctly maps to the desired AWS resource, enabling seamless DNS routing and integration with the specified service.

blocks.llm_summary: The `alias` block in the `aws_route53_record` resource enables the configuration of DNS alias records, allowing users to point a Route 53 record to AWS resources like load balancers, CloudFront distributions, or S3 buckets without specifying IP addresses. It encapsulates settings for seamless integration with AWS-managed resources, bypassing manual `ttl` and `records` configurations, and is essential for simplifying DNS management and ensuring dynamic resource resolution.

blocks.name: cidr_routing_policy
blocks.description: (Optional) A block indicating a routing policy based on the IP network ranges of requestors. Conflicts with any other routing policy. Documented below.

arguments.name: collection_id
arguments.description: (Required) The CIDR collection ID. See the `aws_route53_cidr_collection` resource for more details.
arguments.llm_summary: The `collection_id` argument specifies the unique identifier of the CIDR collection associated with the `cidr_routing_policy` in the `aws_route53_record` resource. By defining this ID, users enable Route 53 to reference and apply CIDR-based routing rules for DNS queries, facilitating advanced traffic management based on IP address ranges.

arguments.name: location_name
arguments.description: (Required) The CIDR collection location name. See the `aws_route53_cidr_location` resource for more details. A `location_name` with an asterisk `"*"` can be used to create a default CIDR record. `collection_id` is still required for default record.
arguments.llm_summary: The `location_name` argument in the `aws_route53_record` resource specifies the CIDR collection location associated with the `cidr_routing_policy`, enabling users to define routing behavior for IP address ranges within a specific geographic or logical grouping. Setting this argument allows users to create targeted or default CIDR records, facilitating precise traffic management and fallback routing configurations in Route 53.

blocks.llm_summary: The `cidr_routing_policy` block within the `aws_route53_record` resource enables IP-based routing by defining policies that direct DNS queries based on the requestor's IP network range. It encapsulates settings for configuring CIDR-based routing rules, providing granular control over DNS responses to optimize traffic management and ensure tailored query handling for specific network ranges.

blocks.name: failover_routing_policy
blocks.description: (Optional) A block indicating the routing behavior when associated health check fails. Conflicts with any other routing policy. Documented below.

arguments.name: type
arguments.description: (Required) `PRIMARY` or `SECONDARY`. A `PRIMARY` record will be served if its healthcheck is passing, otherwise the `SECONDARY` will be served. See http://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover-configuring-options.html#dns-failover-failover-rrsets
arguments.llm_summary: The `type` argument in the context of the `failover_routing_policy` for the `aws_route53_record` resource specifies whether the DNS record is designated as `PRIMARY` or `SECONDARY` within a failover configuration. This allows users to define the priority of records for routing traffic, ensuring that the `PRIMARY` record is served when its associated health check passes, and automatically falling back to the `SECONDARY` record during health check failures, enabling robust high-availability and disaster recovery strategies.

blocks.llm_summary: The `failover_routing_policy` block in the `aws_route53_record` resource configures failover behavior for DNS routing, ensuring traffic is redirected based on the health status of associated resources. It encapsulates settings for managing routing decisions when a linked health check fails, enabling users to implement high availability and disaster recovery strategies by designating primary and secondary endpoints.

blocks.name: geolocation_routing_policy
blocks.description: (Optional) A block indicating a routing policy based on the geolocation of the requestor. Conflicts with any other routing policy. Documented below.

arguments.name: continent
arguments.description: A two-letter continent code. See http://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/APIReference/API_GetGeoLocation.html for code details. Either `continent` or `country` must be specified.
arguments.llm_summary: The `continent` argument in the `aws_route53_record` resource allows users to specify a two-letter continent code to define geolocation-based routing behavior within a Route 53 geolocation routing policy. By setting this argument, users can direct DNS queries to specific resources based on the geographic region of the request, enabling targeted traffic management and improved user experience for continent-level routing.

arguments.name: country
arguments.description: A two-character country code or `*` to indicate a default resource record set.
arguments.llm_summary: The `country` argument in the context of the `geolocation_routing_policy` for the `aws_route53_record` resource allows users to specify a two-character country code or `*` to define the geographic region for which the DNS record applies. This enables targeted routing of traffic based on the user's location, supporting use cases like region-specific content delivery or compliance with geographic restrictions.

arguments.name: subdivision
arguments.description: (Optional) A subdivision code for a country.
arguments.llm_summary: The `subdivision` argument in the `aws_route53_record` resource allows users to specify a specific subdivision code (e.g., state, province, or region) within a country for geolocation-based routing policies. By setting this argument, users can refine traffic routing to target DNS queries originating from a particular region within a country, enabling more granular control over geographic traffic distribution and improving localized service delivery.

blocks.llm_summary: The `geolocation_routing_policy` block within the `aws_route53_record` resource enables routing DNS queries based on the geographic location of the requestor, allowing for region-specific traffic management. It encapsulates settings that define geolocation-based routing rules, ensuring precise control over how requests are directed to endpoints based on the origin of the query, and conflicts with other routing policies to maintain exclusivity in routing logic.

blocks.name: geoproximity_routing_policy
blocks.description: (Optional) A block indicating a routing policy based on the geoproximity of the requestor. Conflicts with any other routing policy. Documented below.

arguments.name: aws_region
arguments.llm_summary: The `aws_region` argument in the context of the `geoproximity_routing_policy` for the `aws_route53_record` resource allows users to specify the AWS region associated with a geoproximity routing configuration. By setting this argument, users can define the geographic location of the resource to influence DNS routing decisions based on proximity, enabling more precise traffic distribution and optimization for latency-sensitive applications.

arguments.name: bias
arguments.llm_summary: The `bias` argument in the `geoproximity_routing_policy` for the `aws_route53_record` resource allows users to specify a numeric value that influences the routing preference for a geographic location. By setting this argument, users can adjust the weight of traffic directed to a specific region, enabling fine-grained control over geoproximity-based DNS routing to optimize performance or balance load across multiple endpoints.

arguments.name: local_zone_group
arguments.llm_summary: The `local_zone_group` argument in the context of the `geoproximity_routing_policy` for the `aws_route53_record` resource allows users to specify a group of AWS Local Zones to associate with the geoproximity routing configuration. By setting this argument, users can control traffic routing based on proximity to specific Local Zones, enabling more granular and location-aware DNS responses to optimize latency or meet regional requirements.

blocks.name: coordinates

arguments.name: latitude
arguments.llm_summary: The `latitude` argument in the `aws_route53_record` resource specifies the geographic latitude coordinate for a DNS record, enabling users to define location-based routing or geolocation-specific DNS behavior. By setting this required string value, users can configure precise geographic targeting to optimize traffic distribution or implement location-aware functionality for their applications.

arguments.name: longitude
arguments.llm_summary: The `longitude` argument in the `aws_route53_record` resource under the "coordinates" context allows users to specify the geographic longitude of a DNS record, enabling geolocation-based routing or location-specific DNS configurations. By defining this value, users can direct traffic based on the physical location of resources, supporting use cases like optimizing latency or implementing region-aware services.

blocks.llm_summary: The `coordinates` configuration block within the `geoproximity_routing_policy` of the `aws_route53_record` resource defines the latitude and longitude values used to specify the physical location of a resource for geoproximity-based DNS routing. By configuring this block, users can precisely control traffic routing based on geographic proximity, enabling optimized user experiences and efficient resource utilization for location-aware applications.

The `geoproximity_routing_policy` block within the `aws_route53_record` resource enables geoproximity-based DNS routing, allowing users to direct traffic based on the physical distance between requestors and designated AWS resources. This block encapsulates settings for defining proximity-based routing rules, providing granular control over traffic distribution to optimize latency or regional access while ensuring it does not conflict with other routing policies.

blocks.name: latency_routing_policy
blocks.description: (Optional) A block indicating a routing policy based on the latency between the requestor and an AWS region. Conflicts with any other routing policy. Documented below.

arguments.name: region
arguments.description: (Required) An AWS region from which to measure latency. See http://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy.html#routing-policy-latency
arguments.llm_summary: The `region` argument specifies the AWS region used to measure latency for the `latency_routing_policy` in an `aws_route53_record`. By defining this value, users can control which region's latency metrics are considered when directing traffic, enabling optimized routing decisions based on the lowest latency for end-user requests.

blocks.llm_summary: The `latency_routing_policy` block within the `aws_route53_record` resource configures DNS routing based on the latency between the requestor and AWS regions, enabling optimized traffic flow to the region with the lowest latency. This block encapsulates settings for latency-based routing policies, ensuring precise control over DNS responses to improve application performance and user experience by directing traffic to the fastest available endpoint.

blocks.name: weighted_routing_policy
blocks.description: (Optional) A block indicating a weighted routing policy. Conflicts with any other routing policy. Documented below.

arguments.name: weight
arguments.description: (Required) A numeric value indicating the relative weight of the record. See http://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy.html#routing-policy-weighted.
arguments.llm_summary: The `weight` argument in the `aws_route53_record` resource's `weighted_routing_policy` defines the relative priority or distribution of traffic among multiple records within a weighted routing configuration. By specifying a numeric value, users control the proportion of traffic directed to this record compared to others, enabling fine-grained traffic balancing for applications or services across multiple endpoints.

blocks.llm_summary: The `weighted_routing_policy` block within the `aws_route53_record` resource enables the configuration of weighted DNS routing, allowing users to distribute traffic across multiple resources based on assigned weights. This block encapsulates settings for defining traffic distribution proportions, helping achieve fine-grained control over load balancing and resource utilization in Route 53.

attributes.name: fqdn
attributes.description: FQDN built using the zone domain and `name`.
